results.title: Xi welcomes Trump to China ahead of high-stakes Putin meeting
results.content: President Xi Jinping personally greeted US counterpart Donald Trump on the tarmac at a Chinese airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders briefly hugging ahead of their highly anticipated meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin. Beijing has indicated the war in Ukraine will not be discussed during the trilateral meeting, but Trump had said the conflict would find its way onto the agenda, something that experts say is likely to please Putin.

results.title: Three leaders, three agendas: Who wants what from Xi-Trump-Putin summit?
results.content: Be it curbing arms sales to Taiwan, bouncing back after a midterms shellacking, or the optics of a place at the table with the world's two superpowers, Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are approaching their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen with starkly different aims and agendas. Here's a look at what the Chinese, US and Russian leaders are hoping for.

results.title: US strikes Iranian island after Tehran targets Bahrain
results.content: The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.

results.title: Why are measles cases soaring in the US?
results.content: The United States has lost its long-held status of having eradicated measles as cases of the dangerous and highly contagious virus soar around the country. It follows accusations by medical experts that US President Donald Trump and his health secretary, noted vaccine skeptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr, have fanned distrust in vaccinations, leading to an decline on the number of children getting inoculated against the disease.

results.title: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond: The surprise casting choice explained
results.content: Robert Pattinson will be the new James Bond, taking over from Daniel Craig in one of cinema’s most iconic roles. Film critic Emma Jones joins Eve Jackson on the arts24 weekly film show to discuss the surprise choice, Pattinson's star power and what he could bring to 007. Plus, they review the latest "Hunger Games" prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping", Lukas Dhont's Cannes prize winner "Coward" and Germany's Oscar entry "Everytime".

results.title: The calisson: A sweet taste of France's Provence region
results.content: If you've ever visited the south of France, you may have come across a calisson. These traditional yellow and white almond-shaped candies are everywhere in the region. We tell you all about them with our guest Alexis Bertucat, head of communication and tourism for renowned calisson maker Confiserie du Roy René.

results.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race in historic victory
results.content: Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's US Senate race on Tuesday, projections from US media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and becoming the first Democrat to win a US ‌Senate seat in the state in nearly 20 years and the first Alaska Native ever to do so.

results.title: 'A not so veiled criticism of the US' as Xi blasts protectionism at APEC summit
results.content: China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism and said regional economies needed to stand up to rising unilateralism in what France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani says was a "a not so veiled criticism of the US". Xi's comments came APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, where a highly anticipated trilateral meeting between Xi, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin is set to take place on Thursday.

results.title: North Korea completes external works on enrichment facility extension, says IAEA
results.content: A new extension to North Korea's Yongbyon enrichment facility has been "externally complete" since mid-October, according to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which relies on satellite imagery and open sources to monitor the country's nuclear programme. IAEA chief Rafael Grossi on Wednesday said expansion of Pyongyang's enrichment programme remains "cause for serious concern".

results.title: 'Extreme wealth can become a type of brain damage': Journalist Alexander Hurst
results.content: An international journalist who poured his meagre savings into highly risky options trading at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic and quickly made $1.2 million, before losing it all again, has spoken to FRANCE 24 about his experience. Alexander Hurst works for a number of media outlets, including the Guardian as a correspondent based in Paris.

results.title: Athlete support under spotlight as South Africa swimmer switches to Netherlands
results.content: South Africa's sports minister said Tuesday he had ordered an investigation into the national swimming federation following the departure of the country's most decorated Olympic athlete, swimmer Tatjana Smith, for the Netherlands. In an emotional video on social media, the 29-year-old two-time Olympic gold medallist announced last week she would no longer represent South Africa at international events because of financial challenges.

results.title: French police hold Paris rally after weeks of protests
results.content: French police staged a surprise demonstration in front of the French interior ministry in Paris on Wednesday, including members of the specialist riot control unit the CRS. It comes after weeks of huge protest marches around the country that have often descended into violence and led to criticism of police over heavy-handed tactics.

results.title: Inside Nigeria's illegal gold mining industry
results.content: Nigerian authorities are attempting to clean up the mining sector in a country whose subsoil is rich in deposits of uranium, gold and lithium. The vast majority of these resources are mined illegally, meaning billions of euros are not included in the national GDP. Two years ago, the Nigerian government launched a paramilitary force, The Mining Marshals, to fight this illegal activity. Our Nigerian team visited an informal mine and then accompanied a patrol of Mining Marshals, here is their Report.

results.title: Is use of AI threatening Nigerian elections?
results.content: With less than two months to Nigeria’s general elections, there are growing concerns about the possible use of artificial intelligence to influence the outcome of the election. Artificial intelligence is being used for various sinister purposes sometimes to influence voters' perceptions. There also appears an attempt to manipulate the voters register. It was recently discovered that the register was bloated with AI-created individuals. France 24's Sam Olukoya reports from Lagos.

results.title: Chinese cars shake up Ivory Coast's auto industry
results.content: In the space of just a few years, more than a dozen Chinese carmakers have established themselves in Ivory Coast and are becoming increasingly visible on the country's streets. How have they managed to win over a growing number of customers? FRANCE 24's Jean Barrère and Eunice Stolz-Masson report.

results.title: 'A masterpiece of the gaming industry': GTA 'most expensive' entertainment production in history
results.content: François Picard is pleased to welcome Olivier Mauco, President of the European Video Game Observatory and Lecturer at Paris Dauphine University. For Spotlight, he discusses the extraordinary anticipation surrounding GTA 6, the game's enduring popularity and the economics of blockbuster video game production. “It's kind of the masterpiece of the game industry,” says Mauco of Grand Theft Auto, whose next instalment has generated considerable anticipation following a 13-year hiatus.

results.title: Pineapple pizza debate reignites after Italian chef sacked in Australia
results.content: An Italian chef in Australia has lost his job after refusing to put pineapple on a pizza - calling it "an insult" to his culture. He then took his case to an employment tribunal, but his claim was dismissed. The case has reignited one the debate over what many, particularly in Italy consider to be culinary heresy. Our colleagues from France 2 report on the fallout from Rome.

results.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins US Senate race in Alaska
results.content: Democrat Mary Peltola ​won Alaska's US Senate race on Tuesday, projections from US media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and giving her party its ninth Senate flip of the midterm elections and a commanding 56-44 majority in the upper house of Congress. France 24's Washington correspondent Fraser Jackson has the latest.

results.title: Trump arrives in China ahead of trilateral summit with Putin and Xi
results.content: Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen, China on Wednesday, ahead of a historic trilateral on the sidelines of the APEC summit with his Russian and Chinese counterparts. The three men are expected to address the wars in Ukraine and Iran as well as nuclear disarmament.

results.title: Rubio says 'zero' information that US tech outages are linked
results.content: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday sought to assure Americans that there’s "zero" information that a cascade of service outages are related to each other or to a malign actor. Outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended to the US National Security Agency on Tuesday, disrupting classified communications.

results.title: Israeli parliament elects speaker backed by Netanyahu opponents
results.content: Israel's parliament voted on Tuesday to select a new speaker opposed to the agenda of Benjamin Netanyahu, a potential first step in rolling back the prime minister's divisive political agenda even as his main rival struggles to form a government. France 24's correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky has the details.

results.title: 'Failures, incompetence, broken promises': Deutsche Bank exposed in major leak
results.content: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 18: A joint investigation following the leak of 15 million documents shows that Deutsche Bank turned a blind eye to the criminal activities of some of its clients. Next, for its 175th birthday, The New York Times has chosen the top 10 stories that made history. Wired is focusing on the moments that defined 2026. Finally, we bring you a story about American parents whose children dream of becoming Formula 1 drivers. But how much does that dream cost?

results.title: Russia, China look to deepen ties at APEC as Trump arrives
results.content: China's leader Xi Jinping urged closer political and military ties between his country and Russia, as he met with President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Wednesday on the sidelines of the APEC summit. It comes as Donald Trump arrives in China for trilateral talks with Xi and Putin.

results.title: Turkish pro-opposition broadcaster taken off air after police raid
results.content: Turkish authorities took pro-opposition Sozcu TV off air in a pre-dawn raid on Tuesday and appointed a trustee to run the channel and its website, prosecutors said, extending a crackdown on the opposition and renewing concerns about media freedom.
